newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-FATHER AND SON FALL FOUL OF STEWARDS.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-FATHER AND SON FALL FOUL OF STEWARDS.

text.p: Trainer Bernard Llewellyn was fined 400 pounds ($672) and his amateur rider son John received a three-day suspension for "schooling in public" in the third race at Bangor on Friday.
Having drifted in the betting from 7-1 to 9-1, Llewellyn's horse Daily Sport Girl raced in the front rank and was in with every chance at the third last flight.
But the seven-year-old lost her place quickly and was pulled up before the penultimate hurdle.
In the fourth race, David Walsh was suspended for two days for using his whip with "unreasonable frequency" on Even Blue, narrowly beaten runner-up to River Mandate.
It was Walsh's second suspension this week. Ironically, the apprentice picked up a three-day ban at Windsor on Wednesday for handling a horse too tenderly.
